title: 'Significant' wind, waves and rainfall forecast for coastal B.C.: Environment Canada
summary: More rainy, windy weather is expected on Vancouver Island and along other parts of the B.C. coast, coinciding with a run of king tides, according to Environment Canada.

image.caption: Rainfall, wind and coastal flooding warnings are in effect for parts of Vancouver Island on Tuesday. (Claire Palmer/CBC)

blocks.text: More rainy, windy weather is expected on Vancouver Island and along other parts of the B.C. coast, coinciding with a run of king tides, according to Environment Canada.
Coastal flooding warnings are in effect for parts of Vancouver Island, the Central Coast and Haida Gwaii
More rainy, windy weather is expected on Vancouver Island and along other parts of the B.C. coast, coinciding with a run of king tides, according to Environment and Climate Change Canada.

The federal department has issued coastal flooding warnings for parts of the Central Coast, western Vancouver Island and Haida Gwaii. It says moderate storm surge and large waves will come alongside very high tides, known as king tides.
Together, they could elevate water levels 20 to 50 centimetres above the highest astronomical tides, Environment Canada says.
A coastal flooding statement is also in effect for parts of the South Coast, with water levels expected to rise and peak on Thursday.
Rainfall amounts of up to 200 millimetres are expected on some parts of Vancouver Island, and some higher amounts are possible locally, according to Environment Canada.
"Rainfall rates will ease Wednesday morning but another potent storm arrives late Wednesday afternoon bringing a new round of significant precipitation and strong winds."
The department is warning landslides could occur in vulnerable areas such as steep slopes, deforested areas or recent burn scars.
Wind warnings are also in effect for parts of Vancouver Island and the Sunshine Coast.
Gusts could reach 110 km/h at times in certain areas. The winds are expected to ease later Tuesday morning.
Local utility outages are possible, according to Environment Canada, and residents are urged to secure loose objects.
The River Forecast Centre has issued a high streamflow advisory for Vancouver Island, as rivers are "expected to rise rapidly in response to rainfall."

The Tla-o-qui-aht First Nation on the west coast of Vancouver Island has issued an evacuation alert for some properties along the shoreline due to flooding. Anyone in the affected area must be ready to leave at a moment's notice.
